title: The Roundabout Has Exits
endLine: Oxaloacetate stays reusable only if what builders take gets refilled.

scenes.tts: Every turn of the roundabout rebuilds four-carbon oxaloacetate. That makes it a reusable platform, not a fuel. So here is a puzzle. If the platform always comes back, why does the cell spend A T P to make more of it?
scenes.caption: Every turn of the roundabout rebuilds four-carbon oxaloacetate. That makes it a reusable platform, not a fuel. So here is a puzzle. If the platform always comes back, why does the cell spend ATP to make more of it?
scenes.visual: Open on the first film's world, unchanged: one large schematic roundabout filling about 70% of the frame, the BLUE station at the bottom labelled 'oxaloacetate · 4C', a YELLOW cart 'acetyl group · 2C' merging from the left, GOLD electron dots orbiting with it, and the slim TEAL carrier lane leading to the right-side 'electron transport chain' block. A full-opacity 'schematic' label sits in a corner throughout. During the first two sentences the cart completes a turn and the blue 4C block slides back into its station. On 'here is a puzzle', a small machine appears on a side road at bottom left. On 'spend ATP', a GREEN 'ATP' token drops into that machine and it stamps out a fresh BLUE 4C block. A large white '?' rises above the station. The road keeps turning slowly.
scenes.narration: Every turn of the roundabout rebuilds four-carbon oxaloacetate. That makes it a reusable platform, not a fuel. So here is a puzzle. If the platform always comes back, why does the cell spend ATP to make more of it?

scenes.visual: Keep the roundabout, cart and side machine moving behind a high-contrast two-second title overlay: 'THE ROUNDABOUT HAS EXITS'. The '?' fades under the title. No separate title layout.

scenes.tts: Because the roundabout has exits. The cycle is amphibolic: it serves both breakdown and building. Citrate leaves to make fatty acids. Alpha-ketoglutarate becomes glutamate and other amino acids. Succinyl co A builds heme. Oxaloacetate itself feeds gluconeogenesis, the making of new glucose.
scenes.caption: Because the roundabout has exits. The cycle is amphibolic: it serves both breakdown and building. Citrate leaves to make fatty acids. α-Ketoglutarate becomes glutamate and other amino acids. Succinyl-CoA builds heme. Oxaloacetate itself feeds gluconeogenesis, the making of new glucose.
scenes.visual: Dim the chain lane to a thin right-edge strip so the frame holds at most six labelled things. Four ORANGE exit ramps grow outward from the same road, one per sentence, each ending in an orange building-site block: from the upper-left road segment marked 'citrate' to 'fatty acids'; from the top segment 'α-ketoglutarate' to 'amino acids'; from the right segment 'succinyl-CoA' to 'heme'; from the bottom station 'oxaloacetate' to 'glucose'. As each ramp appears, a block of the matching road segment peels off the road and travels down it into its site. Label the roundabout 'amphibolic: breakdown + building' on 'amphibolic'. Exit traffic keeps trickling out after each ramp appears.
scenes.narration: Because the roundabout has exits. The cycle is amphibolic: it serves both breakdown and building. Citrate leaves to make fatty acids. α-Ketoglutarate becomes glutamate and other amino acids. Succinyl-CoA builds heme. Oxaloacetate itself feeds gluconeogenesis, the making of new glucose.

scenes.tts: Each exit takes carbon that would have become oxaloacetate. If nothing replaces it, the platform pool shrinks. Citrate synthase, the step that starts each turn, is limited by oxaloacetate supply. So fewer acetyl groups can merge. The cycle slows, and fewer loaded carriers leave for the chain.
scenes.caption: Each exit takes carbon that would have become oxaloacetate. If nothing replaces it, the platform pool shrinks. Citrate synthase, the step that starts each turn, is limited by oxaloacetate supply. So fewer acetyl groups can merge. The cycle slows, and fewer loaded carriers leave for the chain.
scenes.visual: Beside the blue station, grow a tall vertical gauge labelled 'oxaloacetate pool' (schematic, no numbers). With the exits still trickling, the gauge level falls steadily and the stack of blue 4C blocks in the station thins from four to one. On 'citrate synthase', a gate at the station's merge point is labelled 'citrate synthase'; yellow carts queue at it, and only one merges each time a blue block is available. On 'fewer loaded carriers', the faint right-edge chain lane receives only a sparse trickle of teal NADH blocks with gold dots. The road's progress light slows to a crawl but never stops.
scenes.narration: Each exit takes carbon that would have become oxaloacetate. If nothing replaces it, the platform pool shrinks. Citrate synthase, the step that starts each turn, is limited by oxaloacetate supply. So fewer acetyl groups can merge. The cycle slows, and fewer loaded carriers leave for the chain.

scenes.tts: Hans Krebs saw this pool at work in minced pigeon breast muscle. A pinch of a four-carbon acid made the muscle burn far more oxygen than that pinch could explain. Each added molecule joined the pool and carried many acetyl groups through.
scenes.caption: Hans Krebs saw this pool at work in minced pigeon breast muscle. A pinch of a four-carbon acid made the muscle burn far more oxygen than that pinch could explain. Each added molecule joined the pool and carried many acetyl groups through.
scenes.visual: Same world. Temporarily fade the four exit ramps to outlines. On 'a pinch', a small cluster of three BLUE 4C blocks drops from above into the station and the pool gauge rises. Yellow carts that were queuing now merge one after another; the road speeds up. At right, two schematic bars grow: a short one labelled 'pinch alone' and a much taller RED one labelled 'oxygen used'; mark both 'schematic'. On 'carried many acetyl groups', follow one blue block round the road three times, picking up a new yellow cart each time. No pigeon or tissue drawing; blocks only.
scenes.narration: Hans Krebs saw this pool at work in minced pigeon breast muscle. A pinch of a four-carbon acid made the muscle burn far more oxygen than that pinch could explain. Each added molecule joined the pool and carried many acetyl groups through.

scenes.tts: Here is the guiding idea. Oxaloacetate behaves as a catalyst only while nothing is drawn off. Whatever leaves for building must be put back. That refilling has a name: anaplerosis.
scenes.visual: Remove the two bars. Bring the four orange exit ramps back to full colour with traffic flowing out. On the guiding sentence, draw a bright WHITE loop around the roundabout, then let a crack appear in it at each exit as blocks leave. On 'must be put back', a new on-ramp outline appears at bottom left, leading into the blue station, still empty. On 'anaplerosis', label that on-ramp 'anaplerosis · refill'. The pool gauge sits low and wobbles.
scenes.narration: Here is the guiding idea. Oxaloacetate behaves as a catalyst only while nothing is drawn off. Whatever leaves for building must be put back. That refilling has a name: anaplerosis.

scenes.tts: In many tissues, the chief refill enzyme is pyruvate carboxylase. It adds carbon dioxide to pyruvate, making a new oxaloacetate. The reaction uses A T P. That is the A T P spent in the opening puzzle.
scenes.caption: In many tissues, the chief refill enzyme is pyruvate carboxylase. It adds CO₂ to pyruvate, making a new oxaloacetate. The reaction uses ATP. That is the ATP spent in the opening puzzle.
scenes.visual: The side machine from the hook rolls onto the anaplerosis on-ramp and is labelled 'pyruvate carboxylase'. A PURPLE 'pyruvate' block and a GREY 'CO2' block enter it together; a GREEN 'ATP' token drops in; a BLUE 4C block comes out and rolls up the ramp into the station. Repeat at a steady rhythm. The pool gauge climbs. On 'opening puzzle', briefly flash the hook's '?' above the machine and dissolve it.
scenes.narration: In many tissues, the chief refill enzyme is pyruvate carboxylase. It adds CO₂ to pyruvate, making a new oxaloacetate. The reaction uses ATP. That is the ATP spent in the opening puzzle.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Pyruvate carboxylase needs an on switch. Which molecule, arriving at the roundabout's entrance, would make the most sensible signal to build more platform?
scenes.visual: Pause the refill machine with a dim 'OFF' switch drawn on its side. Yellow carts keep arriving at the entrance. Build the large prompt 'What switches the refill on?' at the top, with an answer box containing only '?'. Do not highlight any candidate molecule.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Pyruvate carboxylase needs an on switch. Which molecule, arriving at the roundabout's entrance, would make the most sensible signal to build more platform?

scenes.visual: Hold the prompt and empty answer box for 4.5 seconds. Yellow carts drift in slowly and the road turns gently; the '?' breathes once at two seconds. Nothing reveals the answer.

scenes.tts: Acetyl co A, the incoming fuel. When it is arriving, it switches pyruvate carboxylase on. This is feedforward control. The message reads: fuel is arriving, so build more of the platform.
scenes.caption: Acetyl-CoA, the incoming fuel. When it is arriving, it switches pyruvate carboxylase on. This is feedforward control. The message reads: fuel is arriving, so build more of the platform.
scenes.visual: The answer box fills with a YELLOW 'acetyl-CoA' tag. A yellow arrow runs from the queue of arriving carts to the machine's switch, which flips to a bright 'ON'. The machine restarts and blue 4C blocks roll into the station. On 'feedforward control', label the yellow arrow 'feedforward'. On the last sentence, more carts arrive and the machine speeds up in step with them.
scenes.narration: Acetyl-CoA, the incoming fuel. When it is arriving, it switches pyruvate carboxylase on. This is feedforward control. The message reads: fuel is arriving, so build more of the platform.

scenes.tts: Pyruvate carboxylase is not the only way in. In dividing cells, glutamine is a major source. So a working cycle is a busy hub. Carbon leaves for building, refills come in, and the platform pool holds steady.
scenes.visual: Add a second PINK on-ramp labelled 'glutamine · dividing cells' joining the road at the top 'α-ketoglutarate' segment; mark its entry point 'schematic'. Show all traffic at once: orange blocks leaving by the four exits, blue blocks arriving by the pyruvate carboxylase ramp, pink blocks by the glutamine ramp. On 'holds steady', the pool gauge settles at a level line and stays there. The chain lane brightens again with steady teal carrier traffic.
scenes.narration: Pyruvate carboxylase is not the only way in. In dividing cells, glutamine is a major source. So a working cycle is a busy hub. Carbon leaves for building, refills come in, and the platform pool holds steady.

scenes.tts: So the platform is reusable, but it is not untouchable. The roundabout loads electron carriers and supplies builders at the same time. What the builders take, anaplerosis must give back.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full composition from the hook. On 'reusable', a blue 4C block completes one turn and locks into the station. On 'loads electron carriers', gold pairs flow along the chain lane; on 'supplies builders', the four orange exits pulse together. On the last sentence, the anaplerosis on-ramp pulses and a blue block rolls up it into the station while the road keeps turning.
scenes.narration: So the platform is reusable, but it is not untouchable. The roundabout loads electron carriers and supplies builders at the same time. What the builders take, anaplerosis must give back.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed but still moving world: road turning, orange blocks leaving by the exits, blue blocks arriving by the refill ramp, the pool gauge level. Large white text, centred: 'Oxaloacetate stays reusable only if what builders take gets refilled.' A small Hex mascot waves once; keep the line on screen for the full 3.5 seconds.
